name: Task scheduling (postTask, yield)
plain: Lets a page prioritize its own tasks and yield to input so it stays responsive.
meaning: A site can order its work and split long tasks. It cannot run when the tab is hidden any faster; it only improves smoothness inside the page.

access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
steps: Browser runs it after higher priority work

limits.headline: Can sort its own tasks so the page stays quick when you tap
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens while the page runs and you scroll or tap.
can: Run important page tasks before less important ones
Pause its own long work so taps and scrolls feel smooth
Cancel or move its own queued tasks
cannot: Change what other tabs or other sites do
Skip the browser's own power saving rules
Work in Safari or on iPhone, where it is not offered yet
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge and Firefox support it. Safari, including on iPhone, does not yet.

story.what_it_is: A page can rank its own jobs so it stays responsive when you tap.

marketing.name: Optimize long tasks
marketing.pitch: Chrome's web.dev guide teaches splitting work and yielding so pages respond quickly to taps and keys.

story.for_you: You never see it. A page that uses it responds faster when you tap a button while it is still loading something else.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to meet speed scores that affect search ranking and sales. Giving the browser room to handle taps first makes heavy pages feel quick.

use_cases.example: A busy product page loads reviews in the background so the Add to cart button answers right away.
A browser game keeps frames steady by deferring low priority work, like loading far away level pieces.
A big web spreadsheet recalculates in small chunks so typing is not delayed.
Measurement scripts are queued at low priority so they do not slow the page.
Ads load at a lower priority than the article text.
A feed renders posts slice by slice as you scroll.

technical_bounds: Does not bypass background tab throttling
Support per MDN BCD: Chrome 94 (postTask) and 129 (yield), Firefox 142, no Safari support
